info.title: Elai Public API
info.description:
Every endpoint below is served under `https://apis.elai.io/api/v1`.

## Authentication

Send your workspace API token as a bearer token on every request:

```
Authorization: Bearer <your-api-token>
```

Generate and rotate the token in the Elai web app under **Settings → API**, or through
`POST /generateToken`. The token is scoped to one **workspace** and authenticates as that
workspace's admin user — it is not tied to an individual person, and it carries admin rights
inside that workspace.

A request with a missing, unknown or revoked token gets a bare `401` with no response body.

> **Organizations on the Unlimited plan cannot use the API.** Their requests are rejected with the
> same bare `401` as an invalid token, with nothing to distinguish the two. If a valid, freshly
> generated token returns `401` on every endpoint, check the plan first.

## Errors

Failures carry a JSON body of the shape `{ "message": "..." }`. Validation failures on the newer
endpoints may add an `errors` array naming the offending fields. `401` is the exception: it has no
body at all.

Both render endpoints are **fire-and-forget** — they queue work and return immediately, so a
`200` means "accepted", not "rendered". Render failures surface only through the `video_error`
webhook, never as an HTTP error on the call that started the render.

## Scope

This reference is generated from the running code rather than maintained by hand, so it cannot
quietly fall behind the API it describes. It documents 96 operations across the
`/api/v1` surface.

Endpoints are grouped by subject in the sidebar. If something you need is missing, or an endpoint
does not behave as described here, tell us.

post.description:
Render an existing video that was created before using another request, or with Elai Builder. It can also trigger the re-rendering of failed videos of previous batch requests.

> ❗️ This endpoint accepts work, it does not complete it
>
> A `200` means the render was **queued**. Validation runs after the response is sent, so no render
> failure can reach you as an HTTP status. Failures arrive as a **`video_error`** webhook, or as
> `status: "error"` on `GET /videos/{videoId}` if you poll.
>
> Messages you may receive that way:
>
> | Message | Cause |
> | :--- | :--- |
> | `Slide N is too long. Please limit speech to Xs.` | Speech exceeds the global per-slide limit |
> | `Slide N is too long for this avatar. Please limit speech to Xs.` | Speech exceeds this avatar's own limit, which is lower |
> | `Slide N uses a premium avatar that is no longer available...` | The slide's premium avatar is not available to your plan |
> | `You do not have enough minutes to render this video...` | No minutes left, and the workspace is not allowed to overrun |
> | `Your video has N slides but your plan allows only 3 slides to render.` | Free plans render at most 3 slides |
> | `Video with music should be minimum 2 seconds long` | Background music on a video shorter than 2s |
>
> If you cannot afford to miss a `video_error` — deliveries are single-attempt, with no retry —
> reconcile with `GET /videos` instead of relying on the callback alone.

post.description:
Subscribe to `video_ready` and `video_error`, or replace the URL of an existing subscription. One webhook per workspace: posting again overwrites what was there.

The body is validated strictly — any field other than `url`, `enabled` and `techEmail` is rejected with a `400`.

url.description:
Where we POST each event. **HTTPS only** — an `http://` URL is rejected. URLs containing `localhost` or `elai.io` are rejected as well, so you cannot point a webhook back at us or at your own machine. Maximum 2048 characters.

The schema treats this as optional, but the handler rejects a missing URL, so treat it as required.

techEmail.description: Address we email when deliveries start failing, and again before the webhook is disabled. Must contain `@` or the request is rejected with `Email is not valid`. Maximum 254 characters. If omitted we email the user who created the video instead.

enabled.description: Whether the webhook is active. Defaults to `true`, so you normally omit it. Sending `false` subscribes the URL but leaves it switched off — and a secret set while a webhook is switched off is silently discarded (see Set secret token).

400.description: The URL or the tech email was rejected.

post.description:
Set the shared secret we sign each delivery with. Once set, every request carries `Elai-Timestamp` and `Elai-Signature`; without it, neither header is sent.

> ❗️ Subscribe first, then set the secret
>
> The secret is only stored if a webhook is currently **enabled**. Call this endpoint before `POST /webhook`, or while the webhook is switched off, and the secret is silently discarded — you still get a `200` with the same body, so nothing distinguishes stored from dropped. Deliveries then arrive unsigned while you believe they are signed. Verify by re-reading `GET /apiConfig`.

Use a random, high-entropy string. Setting a new secret replaces the old one immediately, so rotate by updating your consumer first if it only accepts one secret.

Generate a new video from URL, HTML or plain text.

The `{type}` segment selects the parser, and only `html` is special: anything else is read as plain text, which is why an invented `type` appears to work. Reads the speech text of the selected slides and generates quiz questions with an LLM.

Nothing is saved: the questions come back for the caller to place on slides (`PATCH /videos/{videoId}`). `placeAfterSlideId` on each quiz suggests where it belongs.

`notice` is non-null when fewer questions were produced than requested — the slides did not contain enough material. The `feedbackContextId` values are opaque, short-lived identifiers for the generation and can be ignored.

Requires the workspace to have LLM features enabled (`409` otherwise).

notice.description: Set when fewer questions were generated than asked for.

feedbackContextId.description: Opaque, short-lived identifier for this generation. Safe to ignore.

400.description: The video has no slides, or the selected slides contain no speech.

example.message: No text content was found in the selected source. Please select slides with text content or provide a different source.

404.description: One or more requested `slideIds` do not exist on the video.

example.message: Slides not found: 11150988696
LLM service is temporarily unavailable. Please try again.

post.summary: Rephrase or regenerate one quiz question
post.description:
Takes an existing question and returns a new version of it. Stateless — nothing is persisted.

Two modes, with mutually exclusive knobs:

**`rephrase`** — improve the wording. Answer count, quiz type and the number of correct answers are preserved (though which positions are correct may move). Combine hint keys in `instructions` (e.g. `improve_clarity`, `more_professional`). `quizType` and `answersCount` are **rejected** in this mode.

**`regenerate`** — reshape the question, e.g. change type or option count via `quizType` and `answersCount` (`0` lets the model choose). Feedback text is always regenerated. `instructions` are **rejected** in this mode.

`notice` reports `insufficient_data` when the input question was underspecified; the model still runs.

400.description: Body shape invalid, or a field was sent that the chosen `mode` rejects.

post.summary: Render a quiz question to canvas objects (test endpoint)
post.description:
> **Test endpoint.** It exists to verify quiz rendering on the video-render service and is not used by the Elai web app, which builds question objects in the browser. Treat the response shape as unstable.

Turns question parameters into the canvas object that would be drawn on a slide, and returns it alongside a generated slide id.

slide.description: Generated slide id — not persisted anywhere.

clonedCanvasObject.description: The fabric.js canvas object for the question, with `cTop`/`cLeft` copies of its position.

get.description:
Returns the `AuthIntegration` document for the workspace, or `null` when SSO has never been configured.

`config.clientSecret` is always masked as 64 `*` characters — the real secret is never returned by the API.

200.description: The SSO integration, or `null` if none exists.

post.description:
Creates the workspace's single `AuthIntegration` and links the calling admin's user record to it.

Constraints:
- **Enterprise plans only** — any other plan gets `403`.
- One integration per workspace; a second create attempt returns `409`.
- `redirectUrl`, when supplied, is validated against the allowed-host rules and must be a secure URL.
- `config` is validated per protocol; the required keys differ between providers.

A generated 16-character `integrationId` is returned; that value identifies the integration in the SSO login URLs.

403.description: Not a workspace admin, or the organization is not on an Enterprise plan.

example.message: You are not allowed to perform this action

409.description: An SSO integration already exists for this workspace. Use `PUT /sso` to change it.

example.message: Auth integration already exists

put.description:
Replaces `protocol`, `authByInvite`, `anonymizeUsers` and `redirectUrl`, and merges the supplied `config` over the stored one.

Notes that matter in practice:
- **Send the masked secret back unchanged to keep it.** A `config.clientSecret` starting with `***` is dropped before the merge, so the stored secret survives. Sending a real value replaces it.
- Because `config` is merged rather than replaced, keys you omit keep their previous values.
- Low-tier plans get `403`; this check is *not* the same as the Enterprise-only check on create.
- `404` when the workspace has no integration yet.

403.description: Not a workspace admin, or the organization is on a low-tier plan.

404.description: No SSO integration configured for this workspace.

example.message: Auth integration not found

delete.description:
Deletes the `AuthIntegration` and **unsets the `auth` field on every user linked to it**, so those users fall back to email + password and can no longer sign in through the identity provider.

Recorded in the CloudWatch audit log (`api` / `SsoIntegrationDeleted`).

404.description: No SSO integration configured for this workspace.

example.message: Auth integration not found

post.description:
Allocates a GPU host, starts a WebRTC session and returns the SDP offer to answer.

The handshake is: `POST /streams` → answer the offer with `PUT /streams/{streamId}` → trickle ICE candidates with `POST /streams/candidate/{streamId}` → speak with `POST /streams/render/{streamId}`.

Streaming minutes are billed at **0.5×** the normal rate. A workspace with no minutes left is rejected with `429` unless the organization has `allowOverlimit`.

avatarCode.description: Avatar variant code. Must be an avatar with a `realtimeConfig` — see `GET /avatars?realtime=true`.

host.description: Pin the session to a specific GPU host. Leave unset to let the scheduler choose.

200.description: Stream opened; answer the offer to complete the handshake.

id.description: Stream id, used on every subsequent call.

webrtcData.description: WebRTC session description (SDP offer) and ICE configuration from the GPU host.

400.description: `voiceId`, `voiceProvider` or `avatarCode` missing.

example.message: Some of required parameters voiceId, voiceProvider, avatarCode are missed

403.description: The workspace role of the resolved user may not use streams.

example.message: Your user role can not use streams

429.description: No minutes left and overlimit is not allowed.

example.message: You do not have enough minutes to start a stream. Upgrade your account or top up minutes in your profile to continue.

get.description: Asks the GPU host for a **fresh** SDP offer for an already-open stream — use it to recover a dropped peer connection without losing the session. Answer it with `PUT /streams/{streamId}` as on open.

200.description: A new offer for the same stream.

429.description: No minutes left and overlimit is not allowed.

put.description:
Submits the client's SDP answer, completing the handshake.

If the GPU host rejects the answer the stream is closed server-side — but this endpoint still returns `200 {}`, so check stream status rather than treating the response as confirmation.

200.description: Answer forwarded. Empty object; success here does not guarantee the host accepted it.

delete.description:
Closes the stream and releases the GPU host, finalising the minutes charge.

Idempotent in the useful direction: closing an id that does not exist returns `200`. Closing an already-closed stream is an error.

200.description: Stream closed, or no such stream.

400.description: `streamId` is not a valid ObjectId, the stream belongs to another workspace, or it is already closed.

post.description: Forwards one trickle-ICE candidate to the GPU host. Call it once per candidate the browser emits.
Synthesises `text` and streams the avatar speaking it over the open WebRTC connection. Queued behind anything already playing — use `DELETE /streams/render/{streamId}` to cut in.

example.text: Hello, and welcome to the demo.

delete.description: Stops playback immediately and clears anything queued — the barge-in used when a viewer starts talking over the avatar.

post.summary: Get a chat reply for a stream
post.description:
Runs the built-in demo conversational agent over the supplied message history and returns its reply. Backs the interactive demo on the Elai site; it is not a general-purpose chat API and the prompt/persona is fixed server-side.

The reply is returned to the caller — it is **not** automatically spoken. Pass the text to `POST /streams/render/{streamId}` if you want the avatar to say it.

firstMessage.description: Marks the opening turn, which uses a different prompt.

post.description:
Creates a folder in the media library, optionally nested under `parentUploadFolderId`.

Folder names must be unique within the same parent. Only **root-level** folders count against the plan's folder limit.

Callers whose workspace role is `locked` are rejected with `403` unless the `increaseUserLockedRolePrivileges` feature flag is enabled for the tenant.

parentUploadFolderId.description: Parent folder id. Omit it, or send `null`, for a root-level folder — the handler treats a missing and a null parent the same way.

400.description: `name` missing, a folder with that name already exists in the same location, or the plan's folder limit is reached.

example.message: A folder with this name already exists in the same location

post.description:
Lists folders matching a Mongo-style `match` filter, always constrained to the caller's workspace.

With no `match.parentUploadFolderId`, only root-level folders are returned. Pass `match.parentUploadFolderId` to list the children of a specific folder.

On Free, Creator and Team plans each folder carries an `isLimited` flag — `true` means the folder is beyond what the plan allows and is shown but not usable — and limited folders are sorted last.

> `match` is passed to the query almost as given. Treat it as an internal search facility, not a stable filter language.

match.description: Additional filter conditions. `accountId` is always overwritten with the caller's workspace.

post.summary: Get a folder with its children and ancestors
post.description:
Returns one folder with its immediate `children` populated and `parentUploadFolders` — the ancestor chain ordered from the root down.

A `POST` despite being a read: the sort option travels in the body.

200.description: The folder, its children and its ancestors.

400.description: Folder not found, or it belongs to another workspace.

patch.description:
Renames a folder, or moves it under a different parent.

**Rename wins over move.** The two operations are mutually exclusive in one call: if `name` is present the folder is renamed and `parentUploadFolderId` is ignored entirely. Send two requests to do both.

To move a folder to the top level, send `parentUploadFolderId` as `null` or `false`. Names must stay unique within the destination.

parentUploadFolderId.description: New parent, or `null`/`false` for the top level. Only honoured when `name` is absent.

400.description: `name` present but empty, duplicate name in the destination, folder not found, or the destination parent belongs to another workspace.

delete.summary: Delete a folder and everything in it
delete.description:
**Recursive and permanent.** Deletes the folder, every descendant folder, and every asset inside that subtree — including the stored files.

The response returns signed URLs for the deleted assets (`uploadUrls`), captured before deletion, so the caller can offer an undo-by-re-upload. Videos referencing those assets are not updated.

Asset deletion runs at most 10 at a time and is not transactional.

uploadUrls.description: Signed URLs of the deleted assets, taken just before deletion.

example.message: Upload folder deleted successfully

400.description: Folder not found, or it belongs to another workspace.

get.description: Reports how many assets the folder's whole subtree contains and which of them are referenced by videos. Intended as the confirmation step before a recursive delete.

usedFilesInVideos.description: Asset URLs from the subtree that videos still reference.

400.description: Folder not found, or it belongs to another workspace.

get.description:
Returns the path from the media-library root to the folder, ready to render as breadcrumbs. The first entry is always the synthetic root (`{ name: 'Media library', id: null }`).

Each entry carries `isLimited`, flagging folders that exceed the plan's folder allowance.

400.description: Folder not found, or it belongs to another workspace.

get.description: Returns just the names of every media-library folder in the workspace, at any depth — used to check name collisions before creating a folder. No ids, no nesting information.
Returns up to **100** audio assets for the workspace, sorted by most recently updated. Not paginated — `offset` and `limit` are ignored.

Lists `frame` assets — the decorative frames that can be placed around an avatar.

Unlike the other upload endpoints this one is **not scoped to your workspace**: it returns every frame in the installation, because frames are shared catalog content.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring match on frame name.

post.description: Given a list of asset URLs, reports which of them are referenced by at least one video in the workspace. Use it before deleting assets to warn about breaking existing videos.

urls.description: Asset URLs (the stored `url` values, not signed URLs).

200.description: Which of the supplied URLs are in use.

used.description: The subset of the input URLs that are referenced by a video.

patch.summary: Move several assets into a folder
patch.description:
Moves every listed asset into `uploadFolderId`. Omit `uploadFolderId` (or send `null`) to move the assets back to the root of the media library.

The move is all-or-nothing at validation time: if any id is malformed, any asset is missing, or any asset belongs to another workspace, nothing is moved. The `updateMany` that follows is not transactional.

uploadIds.description: Asset ids to move. Must be 24-char hex ObjectIds.

uploadFolderId.description: Destination folder, or `null`/omitted for the media-library root.

example.message: Successfully moved 2 uploads

404.description: At least one asset was not found in this workspace.

uploadFolderId.description: Destination folder, or `null`/omitted for the root.

example.message: Upload moved successfully

post.summary: Upload a background-music track for a video
post.description:
Uploads an audio file as a background-music asset for the given video.

Non-MP3 input is transcoded to MP3 with ffmpeg before storage, so WAV, M4A and similar formats are accepted. The stored asset is keyed by file name: uploading a file whose name already exists in the workspace **overwrites that asset's record** rather than creating a second one.

Send the file as `multipart/form-data` under the field name `file`. Counts against the workspace's asset limit.

parameters.name: videoId
parameters.description: Video the track is uploaded for. Determines the storage path.

file.description: Audio file. Transcoded to MP3 unless it already is one.

200.description: The created or updated audio asset.

400.description: No file supplied, or the asset limit for the plan is reached.

post.description:
Legacy alias of [`POST /videos/copy`](#operation/copy-video) — the same handler is mounted under both paths, so behaviour, request body and responses are identical.

Kept working for older integrations. Use `POST /videos/copy` in new code.

get.summary: Get the player payload for a video
get.description:
Returns the video shaped for the embedded interactive player — the payload the player runtime consumes, rather than the editable video document. Use `GET /videos/{videoId}` for editing and this for playback.

Deleted videos are refused with `403`.

schema.description: Player-shaped video payload: playable slide data, interactivity and signed media URLs.

example.message: Video is deleted

get.summary: Get the source links of an AI summary video
get.description:
For videos generated as an **AI summary of a Panopto session**, returns the original session's name and viewer URL, plus the containing folder and how many videos are in it.

Only meaningful for that one origin: any other video — including everything created through the public API — returns `404`, as does a summary video whose source session details are missing.

originalVideoUrl.description: Panopto viewer URL of the source session.

404.description: The video is not an AI summary video, or its source session details are unavailable.

example.message: Video links not found

get.description:
Lists the times this video was exported to an external system, newest first, with the user who did it.

Defaults to `target=panopto`; only entries matching the requested target are returned. Thumbnails come back as signed URLs. Exports made by since-deleted users show as `Deleted user`.

200.description: Matching exports, newest first. Empty array when there are none.

name.description: Name the video was exported under.

get.description:
Builds a SCORM package for the video and streams it back as a **zip file** (`Content-Type: application/zip`) — not JSON. The package is built on demand and deleted from the server once the response closes.

`passingScore` and `completionRate` are mutually exclusive: send one or neither, never both. Both are percentages between 0 and 100.

The video must have been rendered; packaging an unrendered video has nothing to include.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: SCORM version. Any other value is rejected.

parameters.name: passingScore
parameters.description: Quiz score required to pass. Cannot be combined with `completionRate`.

parameters.name: completionRate
parameters.description: Playback percentage required for completion. Cannot be combined with `passingScore`.

400.description: Invalid `version`, a percentage outside 0–100, or `passingScore` and `completionRate` sent together.

example.message: Passing score and completion rate cannot be used together

post.summary: Inspect a presentation before importing it
post.description:
Uploads a PPTX/PDF and reports how many slides it has and how many of them have no speaker notes to use as speech — the pre-flight check before `POST /videos/from-presentation`.

Nothing is created and no minutes are consumed. Send the file as `multipart/form-data` under the field name `file`.

missingSlideSpeechCount.description: Slides with no speaker notes — these will have no speech unless you supply text.

400.description: No file supplied, or the conversion service could not read it.

example.message: File is missing

post.summary: Apply a brand kit to a video
post.description:
Applies brand colours and/or a logo from a brand kit to the video.

Scope is controlled by the flags: `applyColors` and `applyLogo` choose what is applied, `allSlides` whether it covers the whole video or just `activeSlideId`. **`persist` decides whether the result is saved** — with `persist` false the modified video is computed and returned without being written, which is how the editor previews the change.

Brand kits are plan-gated; the kit must belong to the caller's workspace.

brandKitId.description: Brand kit to apply. Must belong to this workspace.

logoId.description: Which logo from the kit to place.

allSlides.description: Apply to every slide instead of only `activeSlideId`.

activeSlideId.description: Target slide when `allSlides` is not set.

isSaveCustomLogoPosition.description: Keep a logo position the user dragged by hand.

isHandleApplyAllClick.description: Marks the editor's explicit "apply to all" action.

keepSlideStatus.description: Leave slide render statuses untouched instead of invalidating them.

canvasWidth.description: Canvas width the client is laying out against, for logo scaling.

persist.description: Save the result. When false the change is returned but not written.

200.description: The video with the brand kit applied (saved only when `persist` was true).

403.description: The caller may not edit this video, or brand kits are not available on the plan.

get.description:
Returns the video's name and its `VideoEditHistory` entries, each with the user who made the change.

> The handler logs and swallows any error instead of returning one, so a failure produces **no response at all** and the request hangs until your client times out. Treat a timeout as a failure rather than retrying indefinitely.

userId.description: The editing user, populated with `name` and `email`.

get.description: Lists cloned/custom voices visible to the caller — those owned by the organization, the workspace, or the individual user. Standard catalog voices are not included; use `GET /voices` for those.

id.description: Provider-side voice id, used as `voice` when synthesising.

status.description: Lifecycle state; a voice is usable once training completes.

patch.description:
Synthesises a **fixed sample sentence** (translated into the requested locale) with the supplied `stability` and `speed`, so a customization can be auditioned before it is saved. Your own text is not accepted — that is `PATCH /voices`.

Unlike `PATCH /voices` this does not touch the audio cache and always allows premium voices.

locale.description: Locale used to pick the translated sample sentence, e.g. `en-US`.

200.description: The sample rendered with those settings.

patch.description:
Attaches a recording to an existing `Voice` document, names it, moves it to status `2` (submitted) and emails the Elai avatars team to begin voice creation. It does **not** train anything synchronously — turnaround is manual.

Requires the caller's **organization** role to be `admin`; the workspace-level admin that an API token resolves to is not sufficient unless that user is also an org admin.

footageLink.description: Link to the voice recording for the team to review.

400.description: `id` or `name` missing, or no voice with that id.

403.description: The caller is not an organization admin.

example.message: You are not allowed to perform this action.

404.description: Organization not found.

get.description: Lists every saved voice customization in the workspace. A customization is a named bundle of TTS settings (stability, speed, similarity, style) bound to one voice, referenced from a slide via `voiceVariantId`.

post.description:
Creates a named settings bundle for a voice.

Two mutually exclusive shapes, discriminated by `customVoiceId`:
- **standard voice** — send `language` **and** `locale`, and no `customVoiceId`;
- **custom voice** — send `customVoiceId`, and neither `language` nor `locale`.

Sending both forms, or neither, is rejected with `400`. Only the `elevenlabs` provider is supported today.

patch.description: Updates the `name`, the `settings`, or both. At least one of the two must be present, and `settings` is replaced wholesale rather than merged — send all four values.

delete.description: Deletes the customization and cascades: slides referencing it are cleared and the affected cached audio is invalidated, so those slides re-synthesise with plain voice settings on the next render.
